questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The high quality education that Wageningen University and Research offers and the many interesting courses.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The study environment is absolutely amazing. The facilities at the the university, the engaged professors, the critical approach (the social sciences department) I experienced in many of the courses I participated in.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Introductory days and a study advisor/exchange coordinator, that was present always and answered all of my questions very quickly.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It is super difficult to find something nice to live in. Search for something many months before.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
That they need to apply for something many months before, make a profile at
Idealis.nl
and start applying as soon as you decide to go.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: An exchange coordinator helps you with this, very simple.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: It was automatically done, just needed to pick up a student card in Forum.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesfull.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You can always change courses and apply for new courses, leave the ones you have enrolled in if they do not offer you what you want and enroll in a new course in the two first weeks. This flexibility is amazing.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses are very much like at University of Copenhagen. I even enrolled in master-level courses, and ended up with a fine grade. You just have to check what is recommended knowledge in the course guide.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very similar.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 2 semesters

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Environmental Management and Industry 
Principles of Climate Change Economics and Policy
Business, Human Rights and the Environment 
Sustainability Transitions: concepts, issues and indicators 
Capita Selecta: Capitalist Realism

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
questions.answer:
Introduction to Geo-information Science 
Advanced Environmental Policy and Economics 
Cost Benefit Analysis

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: This was the best course I've ever taken: Business, Human Rights and the Environment. The professor was so engaged and the content broadened my perspective on how to find solutions to environmental issues. It is a small class and participation in lectures and debates is expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: So many sports offered by the sportscenter, a lot of parties during the weekend, many activities arranged by ESN to attend and buddy-family-programmes to get you started. Also an AID the first week, which you need to apply for in time!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Visiting Utrecht, Skate Café in Amsterdam (best dance spot in the Netherlands), look for a subrent in Droevendaal, swim in the Rhine, go to the forest!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Stay in Wageningen actually and meet people here. There are so many amazing passionate young people! Otherwise, go around the Netherlands.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I lived in a self-contained apartment, and therefore it was difficult. But then I moved and started doing courses, and then you meet people easily.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Do sports! Be a part of ISOW or ESN! Live in a non-selfcontained place

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the international community here

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
If you want to be in an international vibrant student environment, go! You will meet people from all over the world!
If you want courses with a critical approach (most social sciences and policy) go! 
If you want big city vibes and find small towns boring, do not go haha! But, you might be surprised what the intimacy in a small town brings - it is easier to meet people.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Idealis.nl
- search for housing
Drovendaal group on FB - search for housing
Go have a coffee at Columbus!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I have met

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Not knowing anyone in the beginning, being patient.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
